description: The line plot illustrates the “Harmful with Refusal Ratio” across four different model configurations as a function of input sequence length (x-axis), which ranges from 128 to 1024 in powers of two (128, 256, 512, 1024), plotted on a linear scale. The y-axis, labeled “Harmful with Refusal Ratio,” ranges from 0.0 to 0.5 in increments of 0.1, also on a linear scale. Four distinct lines represent different model-benchmark combinations: Qwen2-VL-7B on FigStep (orange squares, solid line), LLaVA-1.5-7B on MMSafetyBench (green triangles, solid line), Qwen2-VL-7B on MMSafetyBench (red diamonds, solid line), and a fourth model (blue circles, solid line) whose label is obscured in the legend. All lines show an increasing trend in harmful refusal ratio as sequence length grows. At 128, the ratios are approximately 0.20 (blue), 0.15 (orange), 0.06 (green), and 0.24 (red). By 1024, the ratios reach approximately 0.36 (blue), 0.42 (orange), 0.38 (green), and 0.52 (red). The red line (Qwen2-VL-7B on MMSafetyBench) consistently shows the highest harmful refusal ratio across all sequence lengths, while the green line (LLaVA-1.5-7B on MMSafetyBench) starts lowest and remains below the others except at 512, where it briefly surpasses the blue line. The orange line (Qwen2-VL-7B on FigStep) rises sharply between 128 and 512, then plateaus. The blue line increases steadily but remains the lowest among the visible models after 512.
